title: BLD-684: CLI --json Flag for Machine-Parseable Comment Output
description: This tour walks through the addition of a --json flag to the `hlx comments list` command in helix-cli. The host agent runner inside the sprite needs to pull unprocessed comments programmatically via the CLI (execFile), but the existing output was human-readable text that omitted comment IDs. Adding --json enables the runner to parse structured comment data including IDs for cursor-based deduplication via the lastProcessedCommentId marker, without breaking the existing human-readable default output.

steps.description: The `hlx comments list` command was the single file requiring modification for BLD-684. The runner in helix-global-server calls `hlx` via execFile and needs structured output to advance its lastProcessedCommentId cursor. The existing command already had --since filtering and the CommentResponse type already included an `id` field — the only missing piece was a way to emit that data as JSON.
steps.title: Overview: Why this file needed to change

steps.description: The CommentResponse type already includes `id: string` among its fields (along with author, content, isHelixTagged, isAgentAuthored, createdAt). This means no type changes were required — the id was always fetched from the API, just never surfaced in the human-readable output. The --json flag leverages this existing shape by calling JSON.stringify on the full array.
steps.title: CommentResponse type already has id field

steps.description: The --json flag is parsed here using the existing getFlag() utility, consistent with how --since and --helix-only are parsed. No new parsing infrastructure was needed. When present, this flag signals that the caller is a machine consumer (the runner) rather than a human operator.
steps.title: Parsing the --json flag

steps.description: After all filtering (--helix-only, --since) is applied to the comments array, the --json branch checks the flag and emits JSON.stringify(comments) with an early return. This placement is critical: filtering happens first so the runner receives the same subset it would see in human-readable mode. The early return ensures the human-readable loop below never executes when --json is active, keeping both paths cleanly separated.
steps.title: JSON output branch with early return

steps.description: The original human-readable output loop ([timestamp] Author [markers]: content) is completely unchanged and only executes when --json is not specified. This is a non-breaking change — existing scripts or humans running `hlx comments list` without --json see identical output. The runner opts in to structured output explicitly, which is the correct default-safe design for a CLI used by both humans and machines.
steps.title: Human-readable output preserved unchanged

steps.description: The code review artifact confirms the implementation is correct and complete: --json flag parsed at L18, JSON.stringify(comments) at L40 includes all fields (id, author, content, isHelixTagged, isAgentAuthored, createdAt), filtering applied before JSON output, and default human-readable output preserved. No changes were required during review. This satisfies all three acceptance criteria: structured JSON with comment IDs, runner-parseable output, and no breaking change to default behavior.
steps.title: Code review confirmed correctness

steps.description: The complete data flow after this change: runner calls `hlx comments list --since <marker> --json` via execFile → CLI fetches all comments from GET /tickets/{ticketId}/comments → applies client-side --since and --helix-only filters → emits JSON.stringify(comments) including id fields → runner parses the array and advances lastProcessedCommentId. No existing code paths are affected: the human-readable path is unchanged, the API fetch is unchanged, the CommentResponse type is unchanged. The change is minimal, targeted, and the major code paths remain clean.
steps.title: Summary: Data flow and codebase integrity
